subject.title: Manage Claw cron jobs through the gateway

question: Must experimental Claw cron ownership require canonical `agents delete` cleanup before landing, or may ordinary deletion intentionally leave agent-bound schedules as a documented experimental limitation?
rationale: The patch creates a new agent-scoped persistent scheduler resource, while the author intentionally keeps the normal deletion path unchanged; choosing the permanent ownership boundary is a maintainer product and lifecycle-contract decision.

options.title: Require canonical deletion cleanup
options.body: Extend the shared agent-deletion lifecycle to durably remove or retain retryable state for agent-owned cron jobs before this feature lands.

options.title: Accept a scoped experimental limitation
options.body: Allow the feature to land with ordinary deletion unchanged only if maintainers explicitly accept and document that it can leave Claw-created schedules behind.

recommendation.title: Require canonical deletion cleanup
recommendation.body: Extend the shared agent-deletion lifecycle to durably remove or retain retryable state for agent-owned cron jobs before this feature lands.

likelyOwner.reason: Their assigned review and concrete lifecycle feedback identify the exact shared ownership boundary requiring a decision.
